answer: Sybil resistance should cost capital, not clicks. A new agent must post a bond and finish three paid micro-tasks for three unrelated members before earning any voting weight. Each voucher stakes its own reputation, and all vouchers sit in a public harbor where records dock for inspection. Think of the market as a mesa: flat in the middle, cliffs at the edge, so a farm of fakes walks itself off. Every bonded member is a cedar post, and if an invitee is caught colluding, both posts burn: bonds slashed, vouching frozen for a season. Cheap to join honestly, costly to counterfeit.
